observations: Photo 0: a stack of used wooden pallets next to a truck, with one pallet lying flat in the foreground on dirt ground with refuse.
Photo 1: a similar stack of wooden pallets with a silver car and white SUV in the background and a truck chassis on the left.
Photo 2: multiple stacks of wooden pallets under a shelter, with oval EPAL-style stamps visible on several pallet blocks.
Photo 3: a close-up of a weathered wooden pallet side or crate panel with vertical slats and no readable brand.

claims.evidence: photos cannot confirm country of origin; EPAL-style stamps in photo 2 suggest a European standard but are not proof of origin

risks.risk: structural condition - broken slats, rot, or insect damage hidden in the stack
risks.proof: close-up photos or video of every pallet, especially undersides and block joints
risks.if_unproven: priced as damaged or scrap timber

risks.proof: wide shot showing the full stack with all units countable, or seller video counting them

risks.risk: missing heat treatment / ISPM 15 stamps affecting reuse or export value
risks.proof: close-up of IPPC or HT stamps on pallet blocks

risks.risk: EPAL authenticity if sold as branded foreign pallets
risks.proof: clear close-up of EPAL logo stamps
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic unbranded wooden pallet

proof_requests: Close-up photos of the EPAL or IPPC stamps on the pallet blocks
Video showing the full stack and a count of all pallets
Close-up photos of pallet undersides and block joints to check for breaks or rot
response.reason: The item is clearly a used wooden pallet lot; even with unverified condition, origin, and count, it can be priced at its worst case as seen.
